scope: Three controlled lifecycle observations compare production sameCardId/permanent ID, regular movement, battle history, MayNotMove modifier and weapon/device usage before departure, after equipment return and after host return. A fourth plays actual Old Ben and checks that Luke does not rejoin the current battle but has no earlier-instance battle participation history. All four match native. Lifecycle placements are fixture interventions, not claims that return/redeploy cards were played.
references: GameState.addCardToZone assigns new temporary IDs while permanent IDs survive; Filters.sameCardId snapshots temporary IDs.
ModifiersLogic.regularMovePerformed, participatedInBattle, weaponUsedBy and deviceUsedBy index current IDs. MayNotMoveModifier captures target identity.
Card1_100 and PlaceAtLocationFromLostPileEffect/PlaceCardInPlayEffect: actual Old Ben creates new identity without rejoining current battle.
AR pp11,16,24: leaving table, duration, and card/title-level limits; do not blanket-clear every effect whose source leaves.
limits: Ground card instances and attachment handlers, not every pending effect, general targeting/replacement, persona or conversion aliases, or full matches. Stun, Barrier, pending movement/attachments and Lost-visit invalidation use native lifecycle interventions; no fresh complete GEMP card-by-card comparisons for those branches. React physical/title locks preserved. Production admission closed.
